question: What best describes dietary counselling?

options.A: Handing out strict printed diet sheets
options.B: A collaborative process to improve eating habits
options.C: Prescribing weight loss medications for obese clients
options.D: A medical procedure performed only by surgeons

explanation: Dietary counselling relies on working together with the patient to address lifestyle and food choices rather than just handing over rigid instructions. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h1)

question: Why is dietary counselling considered more than just giving a printed diet list?

options.A: Patients cannot read diet sheets in most rural clinics
options.B: Doctors are the only ones allowed to use printed materials
options.C: Printed lists are too expensive to produce in hospitals
options.D: It actively addresses personal habits and lifestyle realities

explanation: True counselling looks at the whole person, modifying behaviors and fitting nutrition into daily living rather than relying on one-size-fits-all handouts. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h1)

question: What is the primary objective of dietary counselling?

options.A: Ensuring patients lose five kilograms every month
options.B: Empowering patients to make informed food choices
options.C: Reducing hospital food service operating costs
options.D: Replacing all prescribed medications with herbs

explanation: The main goal is giving patients the knowledge and confidence to select foods that promote healing and prevent illness. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h2)

question: A patient with newly diagnosed hypertension needs dietary counselling primarily to achieve what goal?

options.A: Eliminate all carbohydrates from daily meal routines
options.B: Switch completely to expensive imported organic foods
options.C: Increase fluid consumption to flush out excess toxins
options.D: Reduce dietary sodium intake to lower blood pressure

explanation: Controlling hypertension through diet specifically targets lowering sodium to help manage vascular resistance and blood pressure readings. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h2)

question: Why are nurses well-positioned to serve as dietary counsellors?

options.A: Doctors are legally barred from discussing food
options.B: Nurses have exclusive training in food chemistry
options.C: They spend the most direct time with patients
options.D: They write the master hospital diet manual

explanation: Continuous bedside contact allows nurses to monitor intake, notice eating difficulties early, and offer ongoing guidance. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h3)

question: Which action demonstrates the nurse acting in a dietary counselling role?

options.A: Performing a surgical insertion of a feeding tube
options.B: Formulating the hospital kitchen's weekly procurement budget
options.C: Explaining how to read local food labels for salt content
options.D: Ordering specialized laboratory tests to check serum lipids

explanation: Educating the patient on practical skills like label reading directly supports behavior change and nutritional health. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h3)

question: What is a key principle of effective nutritional guidance?

options.A: Forcing patients to adopt unfamiliar foreign recipes
options.B: Prescribing expensive imported supplements every time
options.C: Making advice realistic, available, and affordable
options.D: Ignoring the patient's personal food preferences

explanation: Guidance only works if the patient can access and afford the recommended food items in their local community. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h4)

question: Why should a nurse focus on local staple foods during dietary counselling?

options.A: Hospital regulations forbid mentioning international dishes
options.B: Foreign foods are always toxic to recovering patients
options.C: Local staples require no preparation or cooking time
options.D: It ensures the patient can sustain the diet long-term

explanation: Using familiar local foods makes the transition manageable and increases adherence once the patient returns home. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h4)

question: Who primarily provides Medical Nutrition Therapy for complex disease states?
explanation: Medical Nutrition Therapy requires specialized clinical training typically held by registered dietitians for severe pathologies. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h5)

question: How does dietary counselling differ from Medical Nutrition Therapy?

options.A: MNT is solely handled by general ward nurses
options.B: Counselling covers general healthy eating and basic lifestyle guidance
options.C: Counselling is only performed inside intensive care units
options.D: MNT never involves food or eating plans

explanation: Dietary counselling has a broader wellness and prevention focus, whereas MNT is a specialized treatment for specific medical diagnoses. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h5)

question: What factor must a nurse always respect when giving dietary advice?

options.A: The commercial advertising trends on television
options.B: Cultural and religious beliefs surrounding food
options.C: The personal menu preferences of the hospital cook
options.D: International export laws on food distribution

explanation: Ignoring cultural or religious dietary laws alienates the patient and ensures the guidance will be ignored. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h6)

question: What is the consequence of ignoring cultural food taboos during dietary counselling?

options.A: Automatic promotion of the nurse to head supervisor
options.B: Faster recovery due to strict nutritional compliance
options.C: Immediate legal prosecution for medical malpractice
options.D: Loss of patient trust and poor adherence to the plan

explanation: When cultural norms are dismissed, patients feel disrespected and reject the nutritional recommendations entirely. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h6)
